plan.activation_condition: Temperatures remain below optical-phonon activation but are no longer asymptotically small compared with the acoustic-band cutoff, so nonlinearity of the acoustic dispersion becomes measurable while acoustic phonons still dominate.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, mild drift of C_v/T^3 with T can appear at the upper end of the sampled low-temperature window; in holdout extended to somewhat higher but still sub-optical temperatures, the same curvature strengthens smoothly rather than introducing a new branch.
plan.continuation_path: In the limit of asymptotically low temperature relative to the acoustic cutoff, the refined model must reduce to the parent Debye law C_v \propto T^3/v_s^3.
plan.promotion_reason: The dispersion-curvature correction is controlled by an independent acoustic cutoff scale not determined by T and v_s alone in this benchmark; representing when the deviation from strict T^3 scaling turns on requires one additional sampled material/input quantity.
plan.gap_statement: The parent treats the acoustic branches as perfectly linearly dispersing over all thermally occupied wavevectors, forcing an exact T^3 law throughout the sampled regime.
plan.baseline_assumption: Only linearly dispersing acoustic branches contribute appreciably.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite acoustic bandwidth / non-ideal acoustic dispersion causes the low-frequency Debye approximation to bend as thermal occupation approaches a non-negligible fraction of the acoustic cutoff.
plan.rationale: The parent response is a single-gain power law: varying T at fixed v_s always gives the same cubic slope, and varying v_s only rescales the amplitude by v_s^-3. A realistic next refinement is to relax the idealization of perfectly linear acoustic dispersion, which is scientifically natural before optical modes appear. The concrete distinguishing condition is to compare two temperature ranges at the same v_s while holding the new acoustic-cutoff-related condition fixed: deep in the low-T limit the child agrees with T^3, but at higher yet still acoustic-only temperatures the child shows curvature in C_v versus T, i.e. C_v/T^3 is no longer constant. A single refitted parent prefactor cannot reproduce both the asymptotic low-T match and the systematic drift at less-low T because its temperature exponent is locked to 3 everywhere. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. The effect is admissible only when temperatures are high enough to sample beyond the strict long-wavelength limit but still low enough that optical-phonon and electronic contributions remain negligible.

plan.rationale: The parent already captures Debye T^3 scaling and branch splitting, but it retains an independent-branch shortcut in the target mapping: once T, v_s, and v_l are supplied, changing v_s/v_l mainly changes amplitude through 1/v^3 and shifts the longitudinal reduced temperature, while the transverse and longitudinal crossover shapes are otherwise fixed by one shared alpha_nd and one shared beta_nd. A realistic next refinement is to relax that separability and let anisotropy ratio influence the branchwise non-Debye curvature itself. Distinguishing condition: vary v_s/v_l across admissible crystals while holding T/Theta_a in the intermediate low-temperature crossover regime and keeping one global parameter set. The child predicts that two samples with similar low-T amplitude scaling can still show different curvature of C_v(T) versus T because anisotropy modifies the crossover shape, not just its location. The parent cannot reproduce this with a single refit if the observed contrast is a systematic anisotropy-dependent change in bend/steepening over temperature rather than a pure amplitude or simple cutoff shift. This remains scientifically admissible because the effect vanishes as T/Theta_a -> 0, preserving nonnegative heat capacity and the Debye limit, and it is weak or unobservable when v_s/v_l is near 1 or temperatures are too far below the cutoff.

response_change.parent_relation: The longitudinal and transverse branch corrections are independent functions of reduced temperature, coupled only through a fixed longitudinal cutoff rescaling based on v_s/v_l.
response_change.child_relation: Allow the finite-bandwidth/non-Debye curvature of each acoustic branch to depend explicitly on elastic anisotropy through v_s/v_l, so the temperature crossover shape is jointly controlled by T/Theta_a and branch-velocity ratio rather than by branchwise independent denominators.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed low-T Debye prefactor scale, varying v_s/v_l changes not only the overall amplitude through 1/v^3 but also the onset and sharpness of the non-Debye bend; samples with different anisotropy develop different intermediate-temperature curvature that one shared parent parameter set cannot match if it only rescales the longitudinal cutoff.

diagnostic_groups.name: temp_reduced
diagnostic_groups.role: overall thermal occupation relative to the acoustic cutoff

diagnostic_groups.name: anisotropy_ratio
diagnostic_groups.role: elastic branch anisotropy controlling polarization-resolved bandwidth distortion

diagnostic_groups.name: longitudinal_reduced
diagnostic_groups.role: existing branch-shifted longitudinal reduced temperature

contract.activation_condition: Observable when T/Theta_a is no longer asymptotically small but still below order unity, so non-Debye corrections contribute, and when v_s/v_l varies appreciably away from 1 across the sampled crystals or conditions.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, moderate T/Theta_a already reveals anisotropy-dependent curvature differences; in holdout the same mechanism extends to stronger anisotropy or somewhat higher reduced temperature, where branch-shape changes become more pronounced rather than merely rescaled.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when anisotropy-dependent curvature coupling is set to zero, leaving only the current branchwise temperature corrections and cutoff shift.
contract.scientific_mechanism: In anisotropic elastic continua and real crystals, the same bonding/elastic anisotropy that splits sound speeds can also modify how rapidly each acoustic branch departs from linear dispersion near the zone-edge fraction sampled thermally, producing anisotropy-dependent curvature in the heat-capacity crossover.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the quartic crossover terms now depend jointly on reduced temperature and the anisotropy ratio, changing the shape of C_v(T) differently across v_s/v_l rather than applying a uniform gain or a single shifted temperature scale.
contract.assumption_before: Branchwise non-Debye curvature coefficients are fixed constants independent of elastic anisotropy, aside from the longitudinal cutoff shift.
contract.assumption_after: Elastic anisotropy also renormalizes the branchwise non-Debye curvature magnitude through a joint dependence on v_s/v_l and reduced temperature.
contract.parent_reduction: Setting eta_aniso = 0 recovers the parent expression exactly.
contract.observable_signature: When comparing crystals or conditions with different v_s/v_l at the same intermediate T/Theta_a, the child predicts different curvature and bend sharpness in C_v(T) beyond the low-T Debye amplitude and beyond the parent's simple longitudinal cutoff shift; the contrast is strongest for appreciable |1 - v_s/v_l| and fades as T/Theta_a -> 0 or v_s/v_l -> 1.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set can retune alpha_nd, beta_nd, or gamma_lv only globally, so it can shift the overall crossover strength or longitudinal scale but cannot create a systematic anisotropy-dependent family of crossover shapes in which the quartic bend strengthens with (1 - v_s/v_l)**2 across both branches. Separate refits per anisotropy would hide the effect, but one shared parent law cannot reproduce the changed target mapping over varying T and v_s/v_l.

range_suggestions.eta_aniso: Typically between 0 and 3 for a weak-to-moderate positive anisotropy-curvature coupling; values near 0 recover the parent law, and values should keep both branch denominators positive over the sampled T/Theta_a and v_s/v_l range.
